question: An investigator is studying the effect that mutations in different parts of the respiratory tract have on susceptibility to infection. A mutation in the gene encoding for the CD21 protein is induced in a sample of cells obtained from the nasopharyngeal epithelium. This mutation is most likely to prevent infection with which of the following viruses?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Mutation in CD21 gene -> Impaired B cell activation -> Reduced susceptibility to Epstein-Barr virus infection -> 80% CHAIN: Mutation in CD21 gene -> Decreased complement receptor type 2 (CR2) expression -> Reduced susceptibility to Epstein-Barr virus infection -> 75% CHAIN: Mutation in CD21 gene -> Impaired B cell co-stimulation -> Reduced susceptibility to Epstein-Barr virus infection -> 70% CHAIN: Mutation in CD21 gene -> Altered immune response -> Reduced susceptibility to Epstein-Barr virus infection -> 80%
analysis: CD21 protein is the receptor for Epstein-Barr virus (EBV). Mutations in the gene encoding for CD21 protein would most likely prevent infection with Epstein-Barr virus.
